tips.title: Fixing Silvered Decals After They Have Dried
tips.text: Silvered decals happen when air is trapped under the decal. To fix after drying: apply Mr. Mark Softer generously over the decal, wait 10 minutes, then press gently with a damp cotton swab from the center outward to force air bubbles out. Repeat twice more with fresh solution. If silvering persists, carefully slit the decal film with a fresh hobby knife blade in a crosshatch pattern, apply setting solution again, and press flat. Once fully settled, seal with a gloss coat. For stubborn cases, replace the decal and reapply with stronger solutions like Daco Strong.

tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Model Kits
tips.text: To remove old paint from model kits without damaging details, use Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to soften the paint. Apply sparingly with a brush, let it sit for 5 minutes, then gently scrape off the softened paint with a toothpick or dental pick. For tougher spots, use Citadel's Dettol Soap and warm water to scrub gently. Rinse with cold water and dry thoroughly before repainting.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To repair broken photo-etch parts, use CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue like Loctite Super Glue Ultra Gel Control. Apply a small amount to the broken edge, then use tweezers to hold the parts together until the glue sets (about 30 seconds). Once set, use a hobby knife to trim excess glue. For better adhesion, lightly scratch the surfaces to be joined with a hobby knife before applying glue.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To recover a clogged airbrush, first disassemble and soak the nozzle, needle, and other removable parts in Vallejo Airbrush Cleaner for 15 minutes. While soaking, clean the airbrush body with warm water and a soft brush. Reassemble the airbrush, then use Vallejo Airbrush Thinner to backflush the airbrush at 30 psi to remove any remaining paint particles. Inspect the needle and nozzle under magnification to ensure they are clean and smooth before use.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Parts
tips.text: To repair warped parts, gently heat the warped area with a hairdryer set to low heat. Once heated, carefully bend the part back into shape using tweezers or your fingers. Hold the part in place until it cools and sets. For more precise repairs, use a heat gun set to a low temperature and a plastic clay shim to hold the part in shape while heating.
